fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. Each setup script (evals/files/<case>.sh, built on evals/files/sandbox.sh) makes a world in the run's directory: Downloads/, the Apple Music auto-import folder and library under Music/Media.localized/, a NAS staging folder NAS/, and the plugin's config.json under config/, which the session's project settings point MEDIA_MGMT_CONFIG_PATH at (every other MEDIA_MGMT_* variable is blanked, so no real path leaks in). Audio is real: short tagged tones made by ffmpeg, zipped the way stores ship them. The evidence (evals/files/evidence.sh) lists every file added, removed or changed since setup, the whole tree, every MP3's tags as ffprobe reads them, config.json, and, for Apple Music, the stub osascript's calls and playlists.

evals.name: inspect-before-import
evals.prompt: can you check the tags on ./Downloads/Night Drive - Afterglow before I import it into Apple Music
evals.expected_output: A per-track table for the 4 tracks (title, artist, album, genre, track, album artist). Flags two real issues: track 3 (Overpass) has no genre while the others are Electronic, and Album Artist is set to Night Drive on a single-artist album, where the plugin's rule is to clear it. Inspect is read-only: no file changes.
assertions: Presents a table with one row per track (4 rows) showing title, artist, album, genre, track number and album artist
Flags that track 3 (Overpass) has no genre while the other tracks are Electronic
Flags that Album Artist is set on a single-artist album and should be cleared
Does not report a missing title, an artist mismatch or a wrong album name (none exist; every track is titled, by Night Drive, on album Afterglow)
The evidence shows no files added, removed or changed (inspection is read-only)

evals.name: fill-genre-unnamed
evals.prompt: the genre is blank on everything in ./Downloads/Night Drive - Afterglow, fill it in so I can import it
evals.expected_output: The genre is not the user's to guess at and not the assistant's to pick: it confirms the genre is blank on all 4 tracks, fetches the genres already in the Apple Music library (Ambient, Electronic, House, Techno), offers them as numbered options (or a custom one) and asks which. It writes nothing until the user chooses: no file changes.
assertions: The evidence shows no files added, removed or changed: no genre was written to any track
The reply asks the user which genre to use rather than announcing it picked one
The reply offers the genres already in the user's Apple Music library (Ambient, Electronic, House, Techno) as the choices, and allows a custom one
The reply confirms from the tags that the genre is blank on all 4 tracks

evals.name: why-separate-albums
evals.prompt: why does ./Downloads/Summer Sampler show up as four separate albums when I add it to Apple Music?
evals.expected_output: Inspects the folder: 4 tracks by 4 different artists (Kora Lune, Night Drive, Deep Room, Aster), album Summer Sampler, no Album Artist, no compilation flag. Explains that Apple Music groups by Album Artist and falls back to each track's artist, so it splits into four. Classifies it as a compilation and proposes Album Artist 'Various Artists' plus the compilation flag, each track keeping its own artist. Asks before changing anything; no file changes.
assertions: Names the four different track artists (Kora Lune, Night Drive, Deep Room, Aster)
Explains that the missing Album Artist (with no compilation flag) is why Apple Music files it under each artist separately
Proposes Album Artist 'Various Artists' and the compilation flag, keeping each track's own artist
Asks the user before applying the fix
The evidence shows no files added, removed or changed

evals.name: three-artists-one-album
evals.prompt: ./Downloads/Night Drive - Afterglow splits into three albums in Apple Music because track 3 is by Kora Lune and track 4 by Deep Room. Fix the tags so it shows as one album — go ahead and apply it, no need to check with me.
evals.expected_output: Three distinct artists (Night Drive on tracks 1-2, Kora Lune on 3, Deep Room on 4) make it a compilation by the plugin's rule, not a collaboration: Album Artist 'Various Artists' and the compilation flag on all 4 tracks, each track keeping its own artist. Album Artist is not set to Night Drive, even though Night Drive is the most frequent. Re-inspects to verify.
assertions: The evidence shows album_artist 'Various Artists' on all 4 MP3s
The evidence shows the compilation flag set (compilation 1 / TCMP) on all 4 MP3s
The evidence shows each track's own artist unchanged: Night Drive on tracks 1-2, Kora Lune on 3, Deep Room on 4
The evidence shows no album artist 'Night Drive' on any track
The evidence shows no new or removed files
